title: Measure the region or solid that matters
chapter: Measure the region or solid that matters
goal: Worked example: two cuts of the same size with different effects on perimeter.

scenes.visual: Two 6 by 4 rectangles. From the first, a 1 by 1 square is removed at a corner. From the second, a 1 by 1 square is removed from the middle of a long side. Question: "What are the two new perimeters?"
scenes.narration: Start with two rectangles, each six centimetres by four. Cut a one centimetre square from a corner of the first, and a one centimetre square from the middle of an edge of the second. What are the two new perimeters?

scenes.visual: An original rectangle outline with 6, 4, 6, 4 marked. Total 20.
scenes.narration: Each original rectangle has perimeter six plus four plus six plus four: twenty centimetres.

scenes.visual: Corner cut: two removed boundary segments shown dashed, two new segments shown in colour. Count: minus 2, plus 2. Perimeter 20.
scenes.narration: The corner cut removes two one-centimetre pieces of the old boundary, and exposes two new one-centimetre pieces. The change is zero. The perimeter is still twenty centimetres.

scenes.visual: Edge cut: one removed segment dashed, three new segments in colour. Count: minus 1, plus 3. Perimeter 22.
scenes.narration: The cut in the middle of an edge removes only one piece of old boundary, but exposes three new pieces. The change is plus two. The perimeter is twenty-two centimetres.

scenes.visual: Both shapes with their areas: 24 minus 1 gives 23 for each.
scenes.narration: Both shapes have lost the same area. Each has area twenty-three square centimetres. Yet their perimeters differ. The area removed does not decide the change in perimeter; the position of the cut does.

scenes.visual: Line: "new perimeter = old perimeter - removed boundary + new boundary". Notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: New perimeter equals old perimeter, minus the boundary removed, plus the boundary created. Rebuild this, then find the perimeter when a two by one rectangle is cut from the middle of an edge, with its long side along the edge.

notebook_exercise: From a 6 by 4 rectangle, a 2 by 1 rectangle is cut from the middle of an edge, its long side along the edge. New perimeter?
